title: Recognition of known difficult airway before later airway management after introduction of a wristband and electronic alert system: a retrospective segmented time series
abstract: Objective: to assess whether a difficult airway alert system changed documented recognition of known difficulty before later airway management. Design: retrospective segmented time series, January 2019 to August 2026, from a hospital difficult airway database linked to anaesthetic records. Results will be reported after analysis.
introduction: Alert systems aim to ensure that the next anaesthetist knows about a patient's difficult airway, but alerts can be displayed without being read.
methods: Later airway management episodes were identified from the database and reviewed for documented recognition, alert presence and unanticipated difficulty. Quarterly proportions were analysed with segmented regression, listing co-interventions and reporting database capture.
results: No records have been reviewed yet. The report will present episodes per quarter, recognition before and after the change, unanticipated difficulty and database capture.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any change against co-interventions and database capture and will not cite the untraced national figure.
limitations: Co-interventions, documentation of recognition, and episodes outside the hospital.
summary: RECORD-structured draft with results left empty.
